local fn parseObject() -> table<string, any> self.expect(123) local obj: table<string, any> = {} self.skipWs() if self.peekByte() == 125 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 return obj end while true do self.skipWs() local key: string = self.parseString() self.skipWs() self.expect(58) obj[key] = self.parseValue() self.skipWs() match self.peekByte() case 44 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 -- , case 125 then nil -- } handled below case _ then throw "expected `,` or `}` in object at position " .. tostring(self.pos) end if self.peekByte() == 125 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 return obj end end return obj end
local fn parseArray() -> table<any> self.expect(91) local arr: table<any> = {} self.skipWs() if self.peekByte() == 93 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 return arr end while true do Table.insert(arr, self.parseValue()) self.skipWs() match self.peekByte() case 44 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 case 93 then nil case _ then throw "expected `,` or `]` in array at position " .. tostring(self.pos) end if self.peekByte() == 93 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 return arr end end return arr end
local fn parseString() -> string self.expect(34) local parts: table<string> = {} while not self.atEnd() do local b: integer = self.peekByte() if b == 34 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 return Table.concat(parts, "") end if b == 92 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 if self.atEnd() then throw "unterminated escape" end local e: integer = self.peekByte() self.pos = self.pos + 1 if e == 117 then Table.insert(parts, self.readUnicodeEscape()) else Table.insert(parts, self.decodeEscape(e)) end else -- Saule strings are byte-oriented, so multibyte UTF-8 passes through. Table.insert(parts, String.sub(self.text, self.pos, self.pos)) self.pos = self.pos + 1 end end throw "unterminated string" return "" end
local fn decodeEscape(e: integer) -> string return match e case 34 then "\"" case 92 then "\\" case 47 then "/" case 98 then String.char(8) case 102 then String.char(12) case 110 then "\n" case 114 then "\r" case 116 then "\t" case _ then self.fail("unknown escape `\\" .. String.char(e) .. "`") ?? "" end end
local fn readUnicodeEscape() -> string if self.pos + 3 > self.size then throw "truncated \\u escape" end local hex: string = String.sub(self.text, self.pos, self.pos + 3) self.pos = self.pos + 4 local cp: integer = self.hexToInt(hex) ?? -1 if cp < 0 then throw "invalid \\u escape `" .. hex .. "`" end return String.char(cp) end

local fn parseNumber() -> any local start: integer = self.pos local sawDot: boolean = false local sawExp: boolean = false if self.peekByte() == 45 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 end while not self.atEnd() do local b: integer = self.peekByte() if b >= 48 and b <= 57 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 elseif b == 46 and not sawDot and not sawExp then sawDot = true self.pos = self.pos + 1 elseif (b == 101 or b == 69) and not sawExp then sawExp = true self.pos = self.pos + 1 local sign: integer = self.peekByte() if sign == 43 or sign == 45 then self.pos = self.pos + 1 end else break end end local lexeme: string = String.sub(self.text, start, self.pos - 1) if sawDot or sawExp then return tofloat(lexeme) ?? self.fail("invalid number `" .. lexeme .. "`")! end return tointeger(lexeme) ?? self.fail("invalid integer `" .. lexeme .. "`")! end
local fn parseTrue() -> boolean self.expectKeyword("true") return true end
local fn parseFalse() -> boolean self.expectKeyword("false") return false end
local fn parseNull() -> any? self.expectKeyword("null") return nil end end
export class Json -- Parse a JSON document. Returns nil on parse error (or for JSON `null`). static fn decode(source: string) -> any? try return JsonParser(source).parseDocument() catch e: string return nil end end
-- Serialise a Saule value to compact JSON. static fn encode(value: any?) -> string if value == nil then return "null" end return match type(value) case "boolean" then Json.encodeBool(value!) case "integer" then tostring(value) case "float" then tostring(value) case "string" then Json.encodeString(value) case "table" then Json.encodeTable(value) case _ then Json.encodeString(tostring(value)) end end
static local fn encodeBool(b: boolean) -> string return match b case true then "true" case false then "false" end end
static local fn encodeTable(t: any) -> string if Json.looksLikeArray(t) then return Json.encodeArray(t) end return Json.encodeObject(t) end
static local fn encodeString(s: string) -> string local parts: table<string> = {} Table.insert(parts, "\"") local n: integer = String.len(s) local i: integer = 1 while i <= n do Table.insert(parts, Json.escapeByte(String.byte(s, i)!, s, i)) i = i + 1 end Table.insert(parts, "\"") return Table.concat(parts, "") end
static local fn escapeByte(b: integer, s: string, i: integer) -> string return match b case 34 then "\\\"" case 92 then "\\\\" case 8 then "\\b" case 12 then "\\f" case 10 then "\\n" case 13 then "\\r" case 9 then "\\t" case x when x < 32 then String.format("\\u%04x", x) case _ then String.sub(s, i, i) end end
-- A non-empty table with keys exactly 1..#t renders as a JSON array. static local fn looksLikeArray(t: any) -> boolean local len: integer = #t if len == 0 then return false end local count: integer = 0 for k, v in pairs(t) do if type(k) != "integer" then return false end count = count + 1 end return count == len end
static local fn encodeArray(t: any) -> string local parts: table<string> = {} Table.insert(parts, "[") local len: integer = #t local i: integer = 1 while i <= len do if i > 1 then Table.insert(parts, ",") end Table.insert(parts, Json.encode(t[i])) i = i + 1 end Table.insert(parts, "]") return Table.concat(parts, "") end
static local fn encodeObject(t: any) -> string local parts: table<string> = {} Table.insert(parts, "{") local first: boolean = true for k, v in t do if not first then Table.insert(parts, ",") end first = false Table.insert(parts, Json.encodeString(tostring(k))) Table.insert(parts, ":") Table.insert(parts, Json.encode(v)) end Table.insert(parts, "}") return Table.concat(parts, "") end end
